title: a reader of a process decides: a process that is gone answers nil and not an error
intent: The wave repairs the evidence apparatus of the project, and it does not touch the code of the kernel.  The gate of the package of the waves 97 to 99 (2026-11-21) read one line as a refutation: the check of the pilot that ran out of time exited 1.  The check did not fail on its own assertion -- it died on the filesystem.  It looked for the stat file of the process of the server (`file-exists-p'), and the process died in the moment between the look and the read, so the read failed with `file-missing' and Emacs aborted.  The method reads a crashed verifier as an error and not as a proven control (wave 31), and the gate therefore named a refutation where there was none: the claim of the package holds, and the proof of it had crashed.  A false refusal with a false subject is worse than no refusal at all, so the proof is repaired here, and the repair strengthens the proof instead of blinding it.  (1) **One reader of the tree of the processes**: `tests/support/yeah-proc.el' (92 lines, 4 143 bytes) owns the reading of the state and of the ticks of a process; it looks for no file before it reads one (the existence of a file is not a promise that it is still there), it catches the error of the file and nothing else (`file-missing' is a kind of `file-error', and a reader that swallows every error is a reader that is blind), a process that is gone answers nil -- and nil is not the number zero.  (2) **The two checks that read a process read it through that reader**: `check-a-pilot-that-runs-out-of-time-leaves-no-server.el' (223 -> 213 lines, 10 749 -> 10 337 bytes) loses its own `yeah-limit--state', and `check-the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent.el' (186 -> 189 lines, 8 356 -> 8 673 bytes) loses its own `yeah-check--ticks'; the fallback of the path of the binary of Emacs (`/proc/self/exe') is replaced by `invocation-directory', which reads no file of the tree of the processes.  (3) **A server that is gone is a failure that the check names**: the check of the silent server used to read the ticks of a server that is not there as zero and to measure the difference of two zeroes; now the absence of the ticks is a named refusal ('the server of the check is not running'), and the claim is not shown by a process that is not there.  (4) **The proof of the repair**: `check-a-check-that-reads-a-gone-process-decides-and-does-not-crash.el' (260 lines, 12 405 bytes) holds seven assertions -- the state and the ticks of a process that is gone are nil and raise no error, the state of a living process is a letter, the ticks of a living process are a number, the ticks of the reader are the ticks of the process, the reader answers nil for a PID that names no process, and no check of `tests/checks/' reads the stat file of a process by itself.  The fifth assertion is the one that keeps the fourth honest: a reader that answers zero for every process passes 'the ticks are a number', and the check of the silent server is then vacuous, so the check reads the file of its own process itself, without the reader, and compares.  The comparison is a bracket and not an equality -- the ticks of a process never go down (measured on this host: 0 decreases in 2 000 readings), so the answer of the reader must lie between the reading of the check before it and the reading after it, and no clock can make that flaky.  (5) **The claim of the wave is new**: `a-check-that-reads-a-gone-process-decides-and-does-not-crash'.  The two claims whose proof moved into the support (`the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent' and `the-pilot-that-runs-out-of-time-leaves-no-server-behind') keep their id, their text, their falsifier, their requirements and their control; only the scope grows by the file of the support, because the reader of the process lives there now.  The wave touches no file of `lib/' and no file of the site.
objection: The wave repairs a proof and not a feature, and the price is named.  (a) **The repair does not hide the failure of the read**: the reader catches the error of the file and nothing else, and a reader that swallowed every error would be a reader that decides nothing; the check of the repair proves that the reader is not blind -- it reads a living process and its answer is the answer of the kernel, not a constant.  (b) **The repair does not make the checks vacuous**: the absence of the process is a named refusal and not a measurement of zero, so a server that dies fails the check of the silent server instead of passing it.  (c) **The two migrated checks are not weakened**: the claim of the pilot still holds on the state of the process and not on the existence of its directory (a zombie is dead), and the claim of the silent server still measures the ticks of the kernel.  (d) **The claim of the wave is new and does not amend any claim of the package**: the claims of the waves 97 to 99 are not touched at all; the scope of two claims grows by one file, because the reader moved there, and their id, text, falsifier, requirements and control are the same.  (e) **The wave does not close the class of the defect**: a read-only survey of the repository (2026-11-21, the report is in the record of the package) found the same class in six other checks that read 'the process is alive' by the existence of the directory of the process -- a zombie answers that too, so those checks can refute a claim that holds -- and in the shell of the tree (`scripts/lib/tree.sh:46-50', where an awk over the glob of the stat files dies on a file that vanishes and cuts the list of the descendants short), and in the core (`lib/yeah-client.el:62-64', where the port file is deleted by the stop of the service and the client falls where its docstring promises nil).  Those are the next waves; this wave repairs what the gate of the package of the waves 97 to 99 found and no more.  (f) **Two controls of the parent failed the first time and the code was right in both cases**: the mutation of the control C100d changed the condition of the handler instead of taking the guard away (the reader caught the error as before and the check passed -- the control was measuring nothing), and the control C100g looked for one of the two names of the absence of the server while the run produced the other one (both name the same thing).  Both controls were corrected and re-run on 2026-11-21; the corrected controls are the ones that are registered.
refuted_by: the reader of a process raises an error where the process is gone, or the reader answers the number zero for a process that is gone, or the reader answers nil for a process that lives, or the reader answers the same ticks for every process, or the reader raises an error for a PID that names no process, or a check of tests/checks/ reads the stat file of a process by itself, or the server that is gone is measured as a process that burns no CPU, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The wave repairs the evidence apparatus of the project, and the order of the facts is the order of the day.  (1) **The gate of the package of the waves 97 to 99 (2026-11-21, 06:31 UTC) failed with the code 1**, and the log (`/tmp/w97-99-gate.log') holds 163 marks `mathc:': 162 of them are the bite of a negative control (the expected form) and exactly one is a form of a failed positive run -- the red one: `mathc: ./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-a-pilot-that-runs-out-of-time-leaves-no-server.el exited 1'.  There is no mark of the third form (a failed setting of a control).  The check passes when it is run alone: the race appears under the load of the gate.  (2) **The defect was a race of the filesystem and not a defect of the claim**: the check looked for the file of the process and read it after, and the process of the server died in between.  (3) **The repair is a reader that decides**: the reading of a process lives in one place, the absence of the process is nil and not an error, and the absence of the ticks is nil and not zero.  (4) **The proof of the repair holds seven assertions and can fail by each of them**; the bite of the control of the claim was measured by the parent on a copy of the tree (2026-11-21): the mutation of the handler of the reader (`sed -i 's|(file-error nil)|(file-error (error "the reader does not hide the failure of the read"))|' tests/support/yeah-proc.el') makes the check answer 'the state of a process that is gone raised an error: (error "the reader does not hide the failure of the read")' and the code 1.  (5) **Eight controls of the parent (C100a-C100h), all on copies of the tree, 2026-11-21, 0 failures**: the honest tree passes the check of the reader and the two migrated checks (C100a, C100b); the reader answers nil for a PID that names no process (C100c); the reader that raises fails the check (C100d); the reader that is blind fails the check (C100e); the reader whose ticks are zero fails the check (C100f); the server that is gone is named by the check and not measured as zero ticks (C100g); the support is the one reader of the stat file of a process and the two migrated checks go through it (C100h).  (6) **The survey of the class (read-only, 2026-11-21)** counted 42 places of the class and named 19 of them dangerous (9 high, 10 medium); the three that matter are the six checks that read 'alive' by the existence of the directory of the process (a zombie answers that), the awk of `scripts/lib/tree.sh:46-50' that dies on a stat file that vanishes and cuts the list of the descendants short, and `lib/yeah-client.el:62-64', where the port file is deleted under the client.  These are the waves 101 and later, and they are recorded in the plan as the work that the gate did not find and the survey did.  (7) **The finding F39 (the projection of the interface writes the answer `allow-always' as a refusal) is outside this package** and waits for C1: both touch the same record of a decision of a permission.
